title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-06
lineage: SBD Reel master > cassette > DAT > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: Sharp‑ish soundboard tape that captures a strong mid‑1970 set with a smoking Alligator > drums > Love Light sequence and standout Dancing in the Street jam.
ai_review.review: The recording, sourced from an old sound‑board (sbd) master, is surprisingly clear for its age despite a few cuts and missing acoustic material. Musically the show is praised for its deep jams – especially Alligator into the drum solo, the Love Light/NFA/Love transition, and Jerry Garcia’s soaring solos on Morning Dew and China > Rider – making it a favorite among 1970 summer shows.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4‑5 stars and highlight strong performances; recording quality is described as good with minor flaws, yielding an overall rating just above a solid four.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally sharp for a 34‑year‑old tape; occasional cuts and missing acoustic set, but the mix is clear with good instrument separation. No major distortion, just typical age‑related wear.

standout_songs: Love Light > Not Fade Away > Love Light
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows well with seamless segues (e.g., Dire > Alligator, drums into Love Light) and a powerful second‑disk jam marathon; the missing acoustic portion is noted but does not detract from the electric momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers praise Garcia’s lead work – soaring solos on Morning Dew, China > Rider, and tight rhythm throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum segment receives high marks for precision and thunderous energy, especially the post‑Alligator jam.
